en: Sanborn Fire Insurance Map, Delair, Camden County, New Jersey, May 1925, Sheet 1, part 1 (main map)
Sanborn Fire Insurance Map, Delair, Camden County, New Jersey, May 1925, Sheet 2
Sanborn Fire Insurance Map, Delair, Camden County, New Jersey, May 1925, Sheet 3

sheet-1-1.description: The lower two-thirds of sheet 1 of the May 1925 Delair atlas, drawn at 100 feet to an inch below a heavy dividing line; the upper part of the sheet carries the 600-foot key map, the index and notes and is not part of this map. It shows the western end of Delair in Pennsauken Township, between the Delaware River shore on the west and Bannard Avenue on the east, from Engard Avenue south to Derousse Avenue along the bottom edge. The Pennsylvania Railroad (Amboy Division) runs north to south through the middle of the sheet in a strip flanked by two streets both lettered Zimmerman Avenue, with the Delair station and a freight house beside the tracks at Derousse Avenue. West of the railroad Adams Avenue, Delair Avenue and the cross streets Engard, Velde, Curtis and Morgan Avenues are laid out in long narrow lots, mostly vacant, with scattered frame dwellings, coops and garages. In the south-west corner the Camden Water Works' Delair pumping station and a Public Service Company transformer house stand on Delair Avenue near the river. East of the railroad, between the eastern Zimmerman Avenue and Bannard Avenue, are a few more blocks of dwellings with sheds and coops on Engard, Velde and Curtis Avenues. Block numbers are printed with the old block numbers in parentheses. A scale bar and a north arrow sit at the bottom and left; the river bank is drawn as an open curve along the west side.
notes: Zimmerman Avenue is lettered on both sides of the railroad; OpenStreetMap has two ways of that name 45 m apart and both were used as control.
The railroad is lettered P.R.R. (Amboy Div'n); today the River Line.
Delair Avenue west of the railroad has no modern counterpart in the extract.
Fitted rotation (-36 degrees) differs from sheet 2 (-44 degrees): the sheets are drawn square to their own streets.

Map. Two areas: upper third is the key map (600 ft to an inch), index, water and fire notes, not georeferenced; below the heavy line part 1 at 100 ft: western Delair (Adams, Delair, Zimmerman Avs both sides of the P.R.R. Amboy Div., Bannard; Engard, Velde, Curtis, Morgan, Derousse Avs).

sheet-2.description: Sheet 2 of the May 1925 Delair atlas, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and covering the centre of Delair in Pennsauken Township east of the Pennsylvania Railroad. River Road (also lettered Bonsall Avenue or River Road south of Delair Avenue) runs north to south through the sheet and Bannard Avenue runs along the west edge beside the railroad. The northern third, between June Road and Lenox Road with Garden Road, Evaul Road, Wheat Lane and Balfour Road, is thinly built with dwellings on large lots. Pochach Run crosses the sheet from west to east under a concrete bridge on River Road, with the Camden City Water Works power house on large open blocks south of it. South of Delair Avenue the village is laid out in narrow lots along Engard, Velde, Curtis and Derousse Avenues, crossed by Holman, Day and Patton Avenues. Buildings include the Pensauken Township Public School No. 1, the Holy Trinity Church, the Delair M.E. Church, the post office, a few stores and a trolley shelter on River Road; most houses are small frame dwellings with sheds and garages, and the blocks east of Day Avenue are largely vacant. Block numbers carry the old numbers in parentheses. The sheet overlaps sheet 3 along June Road and sheet 1 along Bannard Avenue.
notes: Renamed since: Lenox Road is Lennox Road, Garden Road is Stow Road, Evaul Road is part of Holman Avenue, Patton Avenue is the southern part of Balfour Road, Bonsall Avenue is River Road.
June Road junctions all sat 6 to 7 m off the fit; June Road was left out of the control, so the strip north of Pochach Run is placed by extrapolation.
The school is lettered Pensauken Township Public School No. 1.
Derousse Avenue junctions carry residuals of 3 to 4 m; kept.

Map, 100 ft. Central Delair: River Rd (Bonsall Av), June Rd, Lenox Rd, Garden Rd, Evaul Rd, Wheat Lane, Balfour Rd, Delair, Engard, Velde, Curtis, Derousse Avs, Holman, Day, Patton Avs, Bannard Av; Pochach Run. One part.

sheet-3.description: Sheet 3 of the May 1925 Delair atlas, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and covering the northern part of Delair in Pennsauken Township, between Waterworks Road along the top and June Road along the bottom edge. River Road runs along the west side and Evaul Road, Balfour Road, Eden Lane, Sheppard Road and Haines Road run roughly north to south, crossed by Bridgeview Road, Barrows Road and School Lane, with Wheat Lane running south from School Lane. The sheet is a sparsely built suburban tract: long narrow lots, many vacant, with scattered one and two storey frame dwellings, sheds, coops and garages; the densest building is around School Lane, Eden Lane and Sheppard Road, including a bakery. A fire department building stands on River Road near June Road. An orchard is marked in the east, and the north-east and east edges are marked no exposure. Block numbers run from 15 at the top to 46 at the bottom; the bottom strip repeats the top of sheet 2.
notes: Renamed since: Barrows Road is Barrows Avenue, Bridgeview Road is Bridgeview Avenue, School Lane is Union Avenue, Evaul Road is Holman Avenue, Waterworks Road is roughly John Tipton Boulevard.

The modern streets here do not match the drawn geometry well (residuals 3 to 8 m, the Betsy Ross Bridge approach was built through the area); Balfour Road and the Holman Avenue / Bridgeview Avenue junction were left out and the placement is low confidence.
Haines Road has no counterpart in the modern extract.

Map, 100 ft. Northern Delair: Waterworks Rd, River Rd, Evaul Rd, Balfour Rd, Eden Lane, Sheppard Rd, Haines Rd, Bridgeview Rd, Barrows Rd, School Lane, Wheat Lane, June Rd. One part; modern streets disagree with the drawing by 3-8 m.
